This is for your information and records. Thanking you, Yours faithfully, For Oswal Pumps Limited Anish Kumar Company Secretary and Compliance Officer Encl.: As above Oswal Pumps to set up 1.2 GW TOPCon solar cell manufacturing facility; deepens backward integration across the solar value chain Karnal, Haryana, 10th October 2026: Oswal Pumps Limited, one of India's leading manufacturers of solar pumping systems, solar modules and electric motors, today announced that the Board of Directors of its wholly owned subsidiary, Oswal Solar Energy Private Limited ("OSEPL") has approved plans to set up a 1.2 GW solar cell manufacturing facility based on TOPCon (Tunnel Oxide Passivated Contact) technology. The commercial production is expected to commence by April 2028. The entire output is intended for captive consumption by OSEPL's in-house solar module lines. It is intended to secure a steady, reliable supply of DCR cells and reduce the Company's exposure to spot-market price volatility and supplier-driven commercial terms. It will also extend OSEPL's value addition from module assembly into cell manufacturing. Together, these benefits are expected to strengthen the group's cost structure, competitive positioning in Government-backed programmes, and profitability at the consolidated level over time. Key benefits to Oswal Pumps • ALMM List-II compliance: Assured access to ALMM-compliant domestic cells for modules supplied under PM- KUSUM, PM Surya Ghar, rooftop and other government-linked projects, protecting the company's order book eligibility • Security of supply: Reduced dependence on third-party and imported cells at a time when domestic cell availability is constrained • Cost competitiveness: Lower input costs and freight, strengthening the company's position in price-competitive government tenders • Technology leadership: TOPCon cells deliver higher efficiency and energy yield, enabling higher-wattage, premium modules • Quality control: End-to-end control of cell and module quality, improving reliability and warranty performance of solar pumping systems • Execution agility: Faster turnaround on large orders, supported by in-house supply of cells and modules The total project cost is estimated at approximately ₹456 crore. Of this, about ₹296 crore is proposed to be funded through debt. The balance of ₹159.85 crore is proposed to be funded from the unutilised IPO proceeds of ₹163.04 crore, which were originally earmarked for the Aluminium Frame Facility, the remaining 300 MW EVA Encapsulant Facility and the remaining 500 MW Solar Module Facility through infusion in OSEPL. It is proposed to deploy the Net Proceeds towards the aforementioned solar cell manufacturing facility by Financial Year 2028.
